q: 251. Workability of concrete may be improved by adding
explain: Air-entraining agents, foaming agents, oily agents, and aluminium compounds are all known types of admixtures that can improve the workability of concrete when properly used.

q: 252. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Better grading of the aggregate (proper distribution of particle sizes) results in reduced voids and less water demand, which directly improves and is proportional to workability.

q: 253. Workability of concrete is inversely proportional to
explain: As the time of transit increases, some water evaporates and initial hydration begins, causing the mix to stiffen - hence workability decreases (inversely proportional) with increasing transit time.

q: 254. The shrinkage of concrete
options: is proportional to water content in the mix
explain: Shrinkage of concrete is influenced by water content, cement content, and generally increases (though at a decreasing rate) with the age of concrete - all these factors together describe shrinkage behaviour.

q: 255. Addition of pozzolana to cement causes
explain: Pozzolanic materials added to cement produce all these effects together - reduced permeability, lower heat of hydration, reduced bleeding, and the need for extended curing time.

q: 256. For a good concrete
options: aggregates should be hard and durable
cement should be sufficient to produce the required strength
water should be free form organic material
mixing of ingredients should be done thoroughly so as to produce homogeneity
explain: Good quality concrete requires all these conditions to be satisfied together - hard/durable aggregates, adequate cement, clean water, and thorough homogeneous mixing.

q: 257. For the construction of RCC slab, column, beam and walls, the minimum grade of concrete mixed is used for
explain: The minimum recommended nominal mix for general RCC construction (slabs, columns, beams, walls) is 1:2:4, corresponding to M15 grade concrete.

q: 258. M100 grade of concrete approximates
explain: The M100 grade of concrete (lowest strength grade) approximately corresponds to a lean nominal mix ratio of 1:3:6.

q: 259. M150 grade of concrete approximates
explain: The M150 grade of concrete approximately corresponds to a nominal mix ratio of 1:2:4 (cement:sand:aggregate).

q: 260. Strength of concrete with passage of time
explain: As hydration of cement continues over time, the strength of properly cured concrete continues to increase with the passage of time.

q: 261. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sand and coarse aggregates
explain: Concrete gains its strength primarily through the chemical process of hydration of cement, where cement compounds react with water to form strength-giving hydration products.

q: 262. The nature of fresh concrete is
explain: Freshly mixed (unset) concrete behaves as a plastic material - it can be moulded, placed, and compacted into any shape before it hardens.

q: 263. Too wet concrete may cause
explain: Excessively wet concrete leads to multiple defects together - reduced strength, laitance formation, segregation of ingredients, and lower final density.

q: 264. The process of proper and accurate measurement of concrete ingredients for uniformity of proportion, is known
explain: Batching is the specific term for the process of accurately measuring the quantities of concrete ingredients (cement, sand, aggregate, water) to ensure a uniform mix proportion.

q: 265. Proper batching ensures
explain: Accurate batching of concrete ingredients ensures all these desirable qualities together - economical use of materials, durability, workability, and required strength of the finished concrete.

q: 266. Batching error means inaccuracy in the quantity of
explain: Batching error refers to inaccuracy in measuring the quantities of any or all of the concrete ingredients - aggregates, cement, and water - relative to the intended mix proportions.

q: 267. In the batching of materials, the ingredients should be measured to a tolerance (as a percentage of batch quantity) of
explain: As per standard practice, concrete batching ingredients should be measured within a tolerance of ±3% of the specified batch quantity to ensure acceptable mix accuracy.

q: 268. The process of mixing some mortar in the mixer at the beginning of the first batch concrete mixing is called
explain: 'Buttering' refers to the practice of first mixing a small quantity of mortar in the drum before the main batch, to coat the mixer surfaces and prevent loss of cement paste from the first actual batch.

q: 269. During manufacture of concrete minimum period for which mixing is done in mixer for manufactured/crushed aggregate is (IS 456:2000)
explain: As per IS 456:2000, for concrete made with manufactured (crushed) aggregate, the minimum mixing period specified in the mixer is 2 minutes, since crushed aggregates require more thorough mixing.

q: 270. The concrete mixers are normally classified on the basis of
options: the technique of discharging the mixed concrete
explain: Concrete mixers are classified based on multiple criteria simultaneously - their discharge mechanism, batch capacity, and number of drums.

q: 271. The capacity of concrete mixer is expressed in terms of
options: total volume of concrete produced per day
total volume of concrete produced in 8 hrs
total volume of concrete produced per hr
volume of concrete mix handled per batch
explain: The capacity of a concrete mixer is standardly expressed as the volume of concrete mix it can handle per batch (e.g., a 150-litre mixer, 10/7 mixer, etc.).

q: 272. The objective of mixing concrete materials are the following except
options: coat the surface of all aggregate particles with cement paste
blend all the ingredients into a uniform mass
obtain concrete of uniform colour and grading
explain: Workability is a property influenced by mix proportions (especially water content), not something achieved purely through the mixing process itself, making this the exception among the true objectives of mixing.

q: 273. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: The weight of ingredients of concrete mix, is taken in kilograms
water and aggregates is measured in liters
the finished concrete is measured in cubic metres
20 bags of cement make one tonne
explain: All these statements are factually correct standard conventions used in concrete work - weight in kg, water/aggregates in litres, finished concrete in cubic metres, and 20 bags of 50 kg cement equal one tonne.

q: 274. For batching 1:3:6 and water cement ratio 0.6 both by weight, the quantity of water required per bag, is
explain: For a 50 kg cement bag with a water-cement ratio of 0.6 by weight, the water required = 0.6 x 50 = 30 kg.

q: 275. For batching 1:3:6 concrete mix by volume, the ingredients required per bag for 50kg cement are
options: 70 liters of sand 120 liters of aggregates
70 kg of sand 140 liters of aggregates
105 liters of sand and 140 liters of aggregates
105 liters of sand and 210 liters of aggregates
explain: For a 1:3:6 mix by volume with a standard 50 kg (35-litre volume) cement bag, the proportional quantities work out to 105 litres of sand (3 x 35) and 210 litres of aggregates (6 x 35).

q: 276. The dimension of a 35 litre of forma for measuring aggregates by volume, are
options: length 30 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 30 cm
length 39 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 32 cm
length 27 cm, breadth 27 cm, height 48 cm
length 220 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 40 cm
explain: A standard 35-litre measuring box (forma) for aggregates has dimensions of length 27 cm, breadth 27 cm, and height 48 cm, giving a volume of approximately 35,000 cm³ (35 litres).

q: 277. In case of hand mixing of concrete, the extra cement to be added is
explain: Since hand mixing is less efficient and thorough than machine mixing, an extra 10% cement is typically added to compensate for the reduced mixing efficiency.

q: 278. The process of mixing, transporting, placing and compacting concrete using Ordinary Portland Cement should not take more than
explain: The entire process of mixing, transporting, placing, and compacting concrete made with OPC should ideally be completed within 30 minutes to avoid loss of workability due to initial setting.

q: 279. Placing of concrete should preferably be done at a temperature of
explain: Concrete placing is preferably carried out at a moderate temperature of around 27 ± 2°C, which is favourable for proper hydration and setting without excessive heat or cold-related issues.

q: 280. To prevent segregation, the maximum vertical height for placing concrete, is
explain: To prevent segregation of concrete during placing (free fall), the maximum vertical drop height allowed is limited to about 150 cm (1.5 m).

q: 281. For concerting of tunnel linings, transportation of concrete is done by
explain: For confined and often difficult-access locations like tunnel linings, concrete pumps are the preferred method of transportation, allowing concrete to be conveyed through pipelines to the point of placement.

q: 282. Transport of concrete by pumps, is done for a distance of
explain: Concrete pumps are capable of efficiently transporting concrete over relatively long distances, typically up to about 400 m, without significant loss in workability.

q: 283. 'Tremie' is a
explain: A 'tremie' is a water-tight pipe used to place concrete underwater or in deep foundations, preventing the concrete from mixing with water during placement.

q: 284. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the diameter of the pipe line used for transportation of concrete by pumps does not exceed 30 cm
the slump of the concrete to be pumped should not be less that 5 cm and more
the water cement ratio of concrete to be pumped is kept between 0.5 to 0.65.
number of bends provided in the pipe line should be minimum
explain: All these are correct standard requirements for pumpable concrete - restricted pipe diameter, minimum slump requirement, controlled w/c ratio, and minimizing pipe bends for efficient pumping.

q: 285. Concrete is unsuitable for compaction by vibrator if it is
explain: Very dry concrete mixes are unsuitable for vibration compaction because there isn't enough paste/fluidity for the vibrator to effectively consolidate the mix and expel air voids.

q: 286. While compacting the concrete by a mechanical vibrator, the slump should not exceed
explain: For effective and safe use of mechanical vibrators (avoiding segregation), the slump of the concrete being compacted should not exceed 5.0 cm.

q: 287. Compaction of mechanical vibrations is suitable for
options: all the mixes except very plastic mixes
explain: Mechanical vibration compaction is versatile and suitable across all grades of concrete, all structural elements, and various mix consistencies (except very plastic mixes), making it broadly applicable.

q: 288. Surface vibrator is effective only when the thickness of concrete member does not exceed
explain: Surface vibrators are effective only for compacting relatively thin concrete sections, with their effectiveness limited to a thickness not exceeding 200 mm.

q: 289. A surface vibrator for compaction of concrete is preferred for all of the following except
explain: Surface vibrators, being effective mainly for shallow/thin horizontal sections, are not preferred for columns (which are deep, vertical, heavily reinforced members) unlike footings, slabs, or pavements.

q: 290. Curing
options: prevents the loss of water by evaporation
explain: Curing serves multiple purposes simultaneously - it reduces shrinkage, preserves the desired properties of concrete, and prevents premature loss of moisture through evaporation.

q: 291. The process by which fresh cement concrete is wetted by rain water is known as
explain: Wetting of fresh concrete by rain water is not a controlled/intended process and is not technically classified as curing, wetting (in the technical sense), or raining, so 'none of the above' is correct.

q: 292. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known as
explain: The deliberate process of keeping concrete surfaces moist to promote continued hydration and hardening is technically known as curing.

q: 293. Generally curing is allowed only after concreting of
explain: Curing is generally started/allowed after an initial period of about 24 hours from concreting, once the concrete has achieved sufficient initial set to withstand water application without damage.

q: 294. Steam curing is used in
explain: Steam curing is primarily employed in the mass production of precast concrete elements, where accelerated strength gain is needed to allow rapid mould turnover in factory settings.

q: 295. Steam curing is not used with
explain: High alumina cement generates high heat of hydration rapidly and is sensitive to elevated temperatures, so steam curing (which involves heat) is not used with it, unlike OPC or rapid hardening cement.

q: 296. Curing of pavements, floors, roofs and slabs is done by
explain: For large flat horizontal surfaces like pavements, floors, roofs, and slabs, the ponding method (creating a shallow standing pool of water on the surface) is a commonly used and effective curing technique.

q: 297. Curing period is minimum for concrete using
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly (within 24 hours it can achieve strength comparable to 28-day OPC concrete), so it requires the minimum curing period among the given cement types.

q: 298. Curing of concrete for long period ensures better
explain: Extended/proper curing of concrete ensures improvement in all these properties together - higher strength, better wear resistance, and improved water tightness and durability.

q: 299. Under normal conditions using an ordinary cement, the period of removal of the form work is
options: 14 days for bottom of slabs of spans 4.6 m and more
21 days for bottom of beams over 6m spans
2 days for vertical sides of columns
explain: These are all standard specified formwork removal periods (as per IS code guidance) for different structural elements under normal conditions using ordinary cement, so all of the above is correct.

q: 300. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: water enables chemical reaction to take place with cement
water lubricates the mixture of gravel, sand and cement
only a small quantity of water is required for hydration of cement
strength of concrete structure largely depends upon its workability
explain: All these statements about the role of water in concrete are correct together - it enables cement hydration reaction, lubricates the mix, only a small quantity is chemically needed, and overall structural strength is influenced by workability during placement.
